How Asotin County, Washington, Conducts Tax Sales – A Buyer’s Guide

Asotin County, Washington, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes. If a property owner does not pay taxes for three years, the county begins foreclosure proceedings. The property is then auctioned online, making it easy for buyers to participate from anywhere.

This guide explains how Asotin County tax sales work and what you need to know before bidding.

How the Auction Works

Asotin County conducts tax sales through the Public Surplus auction platform. To participate, you must register on the website before placing a bid. The county provides a list of available properties, including parcel numbers, descriptions, and minimum bid amounts.

The property goes to the highest bidder. Some auctions require a deposit before bidding. If a winning bidder fails to complete the payment, the deposit is forfeited, and the property is put back up for auction.

Tax sales happen regularly, and new properties become available throughout the year. Checking the Auction Calendar frequently ensures you do not miss out on potential opportunities. Property listings and auction details may change, so staying informed is crucial.

How to Prepare for the Auction

Properties sold in tax sales are offered as-is. There are no guarantees about the condition, usability, or title status. Research is critical before placing a bid.

Key Steps to Take Before Bidding:

  1. Review the property list to check legal descriptions, lot sizes, and minimum bids.
  2. Verify the property location to confirm access and boundaries.
  3. Check for existing liens or financial claims that may remain after purchase.
  4. Confirm occupancy status, as legal eviction may be necessary if someone is living on the property.
  5. Understand local land-use regulations, as some properties may have restrictions on development or use.

The county does not allow unauthorized inspections, so visiting the property must be arranged through the current owner.

Payment and Deadlines

Winning bidders must pay the full amount within the deadline set by the county. Payments must be made through electronic funds transfer on the Public Surplus platform. Late payments result in deposit forfeiture, and the property is re-listed for auction.

Important Payment Considerations:

  • Complete payment on time, as there are no extensions or grace periods.
  • Confirm that the county has received and processed the payment.
  • Budget for additional costs, including recording fees and possible legal expenses.

Receiving the Deed

Once payment is processed, the county issues a Treasurer’s Deed to the buyer. This process can take up to 30 days. While the deed transfers ownership, it does not automatically remove any remaining liens or legal disputes.

Steps to Take After Receiving the Deed:

  1. Record the deed with the county to establish legal ownership.
  2. Investigate any remaining title issues or financial claims on the property.
  3. Ensure property access by checking for necessary utilities and road access.

What Happens After You Win

New owners must take full responsibility for the property as soon as they receive the deed.

Essential Tasks for New Property Owners:

  • Secure the property to prevent unauthorized access or damage.
  • Handle any occupancy issues legally, including eviction if necessary.
  • Decide whether to develop, sell, or hold the property as an investment.

Understanding these steps can help buyers avoid unexpected challenges after winning a tax sale auction.
